in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit! To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions.

First, do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 6 years old and lives with me here in the UK. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information! I can see you have a son, Alex, who is 6 years old and lives with you in the UK.

To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask: Are you responsible for Alex's care? For example, do you pay for his food, clothes, and other needs?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely! I'm completely responsible for Alex. I pay for everything he needs - his food, clothes, school things, all of that. He lives with me full-time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's great, thank you for confirming. Just a few more questions to make sure I have all the information I need.

Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him. It's just me looking after him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you. And finally, do you live in the UK? Also, are there any special circumstances I should know about, such as:

- Is Alex currently in hospital or care?
- Is Alex in foster care or an adoption process?
- Do you have any immigration status considerations (such as pre-settled or settled status)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK. And no, there aren't any special circumstances - Alex isn't in hospital or care, he's not fostered or in any adoption process. He just lives at home with me, going to school like any other 6-year-old. Everything's pretty straightforward really.

Great news! **You are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Based on the information you've provided, you meet all the eligibility requirements:

✓ Alex is under 16 years old (he's 6)
✓ You live in the UK
✓ Alex lives with you
✓ You are responsible for Alex's care - you pay for his food, clothes, school needs, and everything else
✓ No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex
✓ There are no special circumstances affecting eligibility

You can proceed with claiming Child Benefit for Alex. 

**Important note:** If you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may need to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge. You can still claim Child Benefit, but you might have to pay some or all of it back through the tax system.

If you'd like to know how to make a claim, you can apply online or contact HMRC for assistance.
